title: Going out as a tenor soloist at Kelly's Stables and the tenor parade
summary: Freeman says he was the first to leave a big band as a soloist, at Kelly's Stables, followed by Lester, Hawkins, Webster and Eldridge in a 'tenor parade'.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But I think that Lester Young had the thing that no one else had, and he was not frightened to come out and play that little tiny sound when everybody else was blowing his brains out. And Lester also had -- he had a marvelous sense of the ridiculous, not in his music, but in his way of life. I will never forget. You see, when the jazz solo thing started, we now left the bands, and I was the first one to go into this. Hawkins was in Europe, mind you, doing
very well, and I had just left the Goodman band, and the people who owned Kelly's Stables in New York asked me if I would want to come in as a soloist and they would put a band behind me.
I was the first one to do this.

Forgive me, when I say the first one. I don't mean that I am looking for any credit. I just mean that it's interesting because then Lester Young was later to leave Basie and he went into the solo field. Hawkins came back, he went into the solo field. Webster left Ellington, he went into the solo field. Roy Eldridge left Krupa, he went into the solo field. All this started and we had a thing called -- we called it tenor parade.
There were about half a dozen tenor players and they all went up to play George Wein's place called Storyville in Boston. So we had the same rhythm section, we traveled alone.
